reason: Adopt the current official Letta application-embedding path as the V2.1 persistent-agent authority: @letta-ai/letta-agent-sdk with its exact bundled @letta-ai/letta-code App Server runtime. Letta owns persistent agent state, memory, conversation continuity, compaction and runtime lifecycle. Yance is limited to exact upstream/dependency pinning, a thin Electron adapter and guarded IPC bridge, binding Letta local-backend storage beneath the existing Yance data root, exposing Letta status/identity in the existing Element Yance Workspace, notices/licenses and compatibility contracts. The legacy letta-ai/letta V1 server is explicitly not authorized. No Yance memory engine, agent state machine, model router, goal engine, tracing stack or second AI frontend is authorized by this package.

ossFit.officialCurrentEmbeddingPath: Official Letta documentation directs application developers to Letta Agent SDK; the legacy letta-ai/letta repository explicitly states that active development moved away from the V1 server and self-hosting now uses the App Server.
ossFit.adoptionMode: Pinned dependency plus thin Electron adapter; SDK-managed local App Server remains the runtime authority.

mandatoryFailureFirstContracts: The trusted base has no exact @letta-ai/letta-agent-sdk dependency, no Letta runtime adapter and no guarded Letta IPC contract before implementation

The implementation must pin @letta-ai/letta-agent-sdk exactly to 0.6.2 and prove its exact bundled @letta-ai/letta-code runtime is 0.30.5; mutable dependency ranges for these two authorities are forbidden
The supported Node floor must satisfy the SDK requirement of Node >=22.19.0; Electron 39.8.5 runtime compatibility must remain explicit
A real local SDK App Server management probe must start on loopback without requiring a model-generation turn and must cleanly terminate

Letta local-backend state must be rooted beneath the resolved Yance data root through LETTA_LOCAL_BACKEND_DIR; default writes to an unrelated user-home Letta tree are forbidden for the Yance-owned launch path
The Electron adapter may expose status, agent/conversation management and future session entrypoints but may not persist a parallel Yance memory or agent-state store
All Letta renderer calls must traverse the existing trusted preload/main-frame IPC boundary and be declared in the IPC manifest; direct Node access from the Element renderer is forbidden
The existing Element Yance Workspace remains the only AI product surface and must show Letta runtime/identity state without introducing a second frontend shell
No model-provider default, Parlant goal policy, LiteLLM/RouteLLM routing, Langfuse tracing or message-send authority may be introduced by this package
Exact upstream repositories, 40-character commits, Apache-2.0 license records and package-lock source integrity must be present before implementation can be considered GREEN
